steps.name: QC and library-size assessment
steps.question: What do library size, gene detection, and sample clustering look like across the 6 HFD and 6 chow liver samples, and how does the low-depth sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) affect these metrics?
acceptance_criteria: Reports per-sample library size (total counts) and number of genes detected for all 12 samples
Confirms sample_01's library size relative to the cohort median and flags it explicitly
Produces a sample-sample correlation or PCA plot on normalized counts showing whether sample_01 is an outlier
Outputs a QC table usable by the differential expression step

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, HFD vs chow
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between HFD-treated and chow-control mouse liver samples (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch), and is the result sensitive to excluding the shallow sample_01?
acceptance_criteria: Runs DESeq2 (or pyDESeq2) Wald test on raw counts with condition (HFD vs chow) as the design, using all 12 samples as primary analysis
Reports full DE table (log2FC, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value) for all ~12000 genes, sorted by adjusted p-value
Repeats the fit excluding sample_01 as a sensitivity analysis and reports how many significant genes (padj<0.05) are gained/lost/reordered versus the full-cohort result
States explicitly whether sample_01's low depth changes the significant gene list materially, rather than silently dropping or silently keeping it
Flags genes with low mean counts appropriately via independent filtering rather than reporting spurious low-count DE hits

steps.name: Pre-ranked hallmark GSEA on HFD vs chow signature
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched among genes changing between HFD and chow in mouse liver, using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the mouse-native MSigDB hallmark gene set collection (MGI symbols) staged in the reference store for Mus musculus — confirms it is present before running and reports plainly if it cannot be located rather than substituting a human gene set
Ranks all tested genes from the primary (full-cohort) DESeq2 result by Wald statistic (or signed -log10(p) x sign(log2FC)) for pre-ranked GSEA
Runs pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea or gseapy prerank) against the hallmark sets and reports normalized enrichment score, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per hallmark term
Reports the hallmark terms passing padj<0.05, ranked by NES, with direction (up in HFD vs up in chow) stated explicitly
Cross-checks top hallmark results against the sensitivity DE run (excluding sample_01) qualitatively and notes if any top pathway's significance depends on the shallow sample

plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 mouse liver samples, mouse gene symbols), 6 HFD vs 6 chow, unpaired single batch. The profile flags sample_01 with a library size ~4x below median, which threatens both normalization and the false-discovery structure of a standard DESeq2 fit, so QC and an explicit low-depth-sample sensitivity check come before the differential expression call. Track 1 runs QC, DESeq2 differential expression (Wald test, HFD vs chow, with and without sample_01 to test robustness), and reports the DE gene table. Track 2 takes the DESeq2 ranked statistic and runs pre-ranked GSEA against the MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (the only hallmark collection staged for this organism) to answer which hallmark pathways change. Both tracks stay in mouse gene-symbol space throughout since the reference hallmark set is already MGI-mapped for Mus musculus — no cross-species ID mapping is needed given mouse-native counts and a mouse-native hallmark file.
